source.title: Benchmarking Transformers-based models on French Spoken Language Understanding tasks
source.authors: Oralie Cattan; Sahar Ghannay; Christophe Servan; Sophie Rosset

record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream SLU performance across pretrained models of different parameter counts, but it does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit scaling curves.
record.gate_note: The MEDIA and ATIS-FR scores bear on downstream performance versus model scale (V6). The study does not measure held-out cross-entropy, scaling-law fit or extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or architecture effects under fixed parameter count. Ecological cost measurements are not results on these claim versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks French SLU downstream scores for models of different size and pretraining-data volume, so it bears on V6 in a new setting. Only a few within-family pairs isolate scale: CamemBERT base vs large on CCNet 135 Gb, XLM-R base vs large, and CamemBERT base on 4 Gb vs about 135 Gb. Scale was not the study's aim, there are only two points per family, and no fit or loss is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that compact FrALBERT reaches results comparable to bigger models with far lower energy and CO2 use. CamemBERT models give the best CER. The volume of pretraining data, not model size, drives the main differences between models. The benefit of compact models depends on the compression method: distillation underperforms.
record.recipe_differences: A downstream fine-tuning and evaluation benchmark across existing pretrained models, not a language-model scaling-law experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The study attributes differences to model characteristics and pretraining data; it notes comparable results for FrALBERT and CamemBERT models trained on Wikipedia data, and different outcomes across tasks and models.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning and inference energy and CO2 rise with parameter count. FrALBERT's inference impact is more than 5x lower than the large models'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream compute cost scales with parameters while SLU accuracy saturates.

record.problems: No controlled parameter-count or compute sweep; models differ in architecture, pretraining data, objective, and vocabulary. No pretraining losses or scaling-law fits are reported. The reported confidence intervals are used to mark significance, but per-score uncertainty values are not given in Table 2.

untested.parts: Predictability of downstream scores (no fit, only two points per family) and their relation to pretraining loss.

missing.what: A qualitative claim that models pretrained on the biggest corpora handle infrequent labels best, with no per-label numbers given.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's single V6 label over cross-family rows was replaced with within-family pair comparisons. The cross-family rows are confounded by data, objective and vocabulary, so they were unlinked. Significance stars are ambiguous in the extracted table layout.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Controlled comparisons of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Scaling-law form in other modalities or training regimes.
No pretraining-loss comparison, controlled size sweep, or predictive fit; it tests downstream scores across a heterogeneous set of pretrained models.
The study does not fit or compare scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations.

relationships.condition: CamemBERT base→large (110M→335M, same CCNet 135 Gb data) on MEDIA
relationships.reason: The larger model is slightly worse: F1 89.2 vs 89.9 and CER 7.8 vs 7.5 (r3, r4).
relationships.display_finding: F1 fell from 89.9 to 89.2 and CER rose from 7.5 to 7.8 when model size increased on the same training data.

relationships.condition: Parameter doubling within families on ATIS-FR and XLM-R on MEDIA
relationships.reason: Gains are small or nil. CamemBERT large gets ATIS-FR CER 3.3 vs 3.7 but flat F1 (r29, r30). XLM-R large shows unstarred differences under 0.5 point (r19, r20, r45, r46).
relationships.display_finding: CamemBERT large reduces ATIS-FR CER from 3.7 to 3.3 with unchanged F1, while XLM-R large differs by less than 0.5 point without reported significance.

relationships.condition: About 30x more pretraining data for CamemBERT base (4 Gb vs 135–138 Gb)
relationships.reason: MEDIA CER improves by 0.4–0.8 points (r6, r8), but F1 and ATIS-FR scores stay flat (r5, r7, r31–r34).
relationships.display_finding: MEDIA CER improves by 0.4–0.8 points, while F1 and ATIS-FR scores remain flat.

relationships.condition: 12M FrALBERT vs 110M CamemBERT, both on Wiki 4 Gb (architecture confounded)
relationships.reason: A 9x parameter difference changes scores by 0.3 points or less (r13, r14, r39, r40).
relationships.display_finding: A ninefold parameter difference changes scores by 0.3 points or less, although architecture also differs.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: French MEDIA and ATIS-FR downstream SLU benchmarks across the compared pretrained models
reader_labels.reason: The study reports comparable results for compact and larger models and says it does not observe a strong broad trend between compact and larger models; model/data differences complicate any scale-based prediction (rows r8, r15, r16, r29, r30, r41, r42).
